lines.caption: Which digit lands in spot number two thousand twenty-six? No need to write them all!

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's count smart, not hard.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's count smart, not hard.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: The whole numbers are written in order, with no spaces. One, two, three, and so on.
lines.caption: The whole numbers are written in order, with no spaces. One, two, three, and so on.

lines.text: After nine comes one zero, then one one, and the digits keep running together.
lines.caption: After nine comes one zero, then one one, and the digits keep running together.

lines.text: What is the two thousand twenty-sixth digit?
lines.caption: What is the two thousand twenty-sixth digit?

lines.text: Here are the five choices.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices.

lines.text: Each spot holds one digit. Spots ten and eleven hold the one and the zero of ten.
lines.caption: Each spot holds one digit. Spots ten and eleven hold the one and the zero of ten.

lines.text: Small numbers use one digit each. Bigger numbers use two, then three.
lines.caption: Small numbers use one digit each. Bigger numbers use two, then three.

lines.text: We need two things: which number covers spot two thousand twenty-six, and which of its digits it is.
lines.caption: We need two things: which number covers spot two thousand twenty-six, and which of its digits it is.

lines.text: Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Let's count the digits in blocks.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Let's count the digits in blocks.

lines.text: One to nine: nine numbers, one digit each. That's nine digits.
lines.caption: One to nine: nine numbers, one digit each. That's nine digits.

lines.text: Ten to ninety-nine: that's ninety numbers. Ninety-nine minus ten, plus one.
lines.caption: Ten to ninety-nine: that's ninety numbers. Ninety-nine minus ten, plus one.

lines.text: We add one because we count both ten and ninety-nine.
lines.caption: We add one because we count both ten and ninety-nine.

lines.text: Each one has two digits, so that's one hundred eighty digits.
lines.caption: Each one has two digits, so that's one hundred eighty digits.

lines.text: So far: nine plus one hundred eighty, one hundred eighty-nine digits.
lines.caption: So far: nine plus one hundred eighty, one hundred eighty-nine digits.

lines.text: Spot two thousand twenty-six is still ahead. We've used one hundred eighty-nine digits.
lines.caption: Spot two thousand twenty-six is still ahead. We've used one hundred eighty-nine digits.

lines.text: Two thousand twenty-six minus one hundred eighty-nine is one thousand eight hundred thirty-seven.
lines.caption: Two thousand twenty-six minus one hundred eighty-nine is one thousand eight hundred thirty-seven.

lines.text: Now every number has three digits. So divide one thousand eight hundred thirty-seven by three.
lines.caption: Now every number has three digits. So divide one thousand eight hundred thirty-seven by three.

lines.text: That's six hundred twelve, remainder one.
lines.caption: That's six hundred twelve, remainder one.

lines.text: So six hundred twelve full three-digit numbers fit, starting at one hundred.
lines.caption: So six hundred twelve full three-digit numbers fit, starting at one hundred.

lines.text: Careful here! They run from one hundred up to seven hundred eleven.
lines.caption: Careful here! They run from one hundred up to seven hundred eleven.

lines.text: Six hundred twelve numbers use one thousand eight hundred thirty-six digits.
lines.caption: Six hundred twelve numbers use one thousand eight hundred thirty-six digits.

lines.text: That reaches spot two thousand twenty-five, the last digit of seven hundred eleven.
lines.caption: That reaches spot two thousand twenty-five, the last digit of seven hundred eleven.

lines.text: The remainder one means one more digit: the first digit of the next number, seven hundred twelve.
lines.caption: The remainder one means one more digit: the first digit of the next number, seven hundred twelve.

lines.text: The two thousand twenty-sixth digit is seven. That's Choice D!
lines.caption: The two thousand twenty-sixth digit is seven. That's Choice D!

lines.text: Here's another way. Every hundred three-digit numbers uses three hundred digits.
lines.caption: Here's another way. Every hundred three-digit numbers uses three hundred digits.

lines.text: Start at one hundred eighty-nine, and jump by three hundreds.
lines.caption: Start at one hundred eighty-nine, and jump by three hundreds.

lines.text: By the end of six hundred ninety-nine, we've used one thousand nine hundred eighty-nine digits.
lines.caption: By the end of six hundred ninety-nine, we've used one thousand nine hundred eighty-nine digits.

lines.text: The next jump would pass two thousand twenty-six. So our digit is in the seven hundreds!
lines.caption: The next jump would pass two thousand twenty-six. So our digit is in the seven hundreds!

lines.text: Two thousand twenty-six minus one thousand nine hundred eighty-nine is thirty-seven.
lines.caption: Two thousand twenty-six minus one thousand nine hundred eighty-nine is thirty-seven.

lines.text: That's twelve threes, plus one.
lines.caption: That's twelve threes, plus one.

lines.text: Twelve numbers, seven hundred through seven hundred eleven. Then one more digit.
lines.caption: Twelve numbers, seven hundred through seven hundred eleven. Then one more digit.

lines.text: It's the first digit of seven hundred twelve. Seven again!
lines.caption: It's the first digit of seven hundred twelve. Seven again!

lines.text: When would you pick this way? When the target is far away. Big jumps first, then small steps.
lines.caption: When would you pick this way? When the target is far away. Big jumps first, then small steps.

lines.text: Now the traps. Choice A, one, is the middle digit of seven hundred twelve.
lines.caption: Now the traps. Choice A, one, is the middle digit of seven hundred twelve.

lines.text: That reads the wrong spot inside the number.
lines.caption: That reads the wrong spot inside the number.

lines.text: Choice B, two, is the last digit. Same mistake: the remainder one means the FIRST digit.
lines.caption: Choice B, two, is the last digit. Same mistake: the remainder one means the FIRST digit.

lines.text: Choice C, six, is what you'd get if you forgot that three-digit numbers start at one hundred.
lines.caption: Choice C, six, is what you'd get if you forgot that three-digit numbers start at one hundred.

lines.text: Count from zero instead of one hundred, and the next number would be six hundred twelve.
lines.caption: Count from zero instead of one hundred, and the next number would be six hundred twelve.

lines.text: Choice E, eight, can't happen. Our digit is the first digit of a number in the seven hundreds.
lines.caption: Choice E, eight, can't happen. Our digit is the first digit of a number in the seven hundreds.

lines.text: So it must be seven.
lines.caption: So it must be seven.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Same long row of digits.

lines.text: What is the digit in spot one thousand?
lines.caption: What is the digit in spot one thousand?

lines.text: One thousand minus one hundred eighty-nine is eight hundred eleven.
lines.caption: One thousand minus one hundred eighty-nine is eight hundred eleven.

lines.text: Eight hundred eleven divided by three is two hundred seventy, remainder one.
lines.caption: Eight hundred eleven divided by three is two hundred seventy, remainder one.

lines.text: Two hundred seventy numbers run from one hundred to three hundred sixty-nine.
lines.caption: Two hundred seventy numbers run from one hundred to three hundred sixty-nine.

lines.text: The remainder one is the first digit of the next number, three hundred seventy.
lines.caption: The remainder one is the first digit of the next number, three hundred seventy.

lines.text: So the digit in spot one thousand is three!
lines.caption: So the digit in spot one thousand is three!

lines.text: If you got three, brilliant counting!
lines.caption: If you got three, brilliant counting!

lines.text: Here's the big idea to remember.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea to remember.

lines.text: Count the digits block by block, and subtract what's used up.
lines.caption: Count the digits block by block, and subtract what's used up.

lines.text: Then divide by the digits per number. How many times it goes in finds the number.
lines.caption: Then divide by the digits per number. How many times it goes in finds the number.

lines.text: The remainder finds the digit inside it.
lines.caption: The remainder finds the digit inside it.
